title: Variant interchange vetter and tokenizer/context sync for routing fallbacks
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: When a request is routed to fallback model variants (region or tier-based), subtle differences in tokenizer behavior, KV cache layout, and tooling-level contracts (function calling/structured outputs) cause user-visible regressions. This ticket coordinates a targeted maintenance sweep to update the compatibility matrix, expand automated vetting, and add runtime guards so routing fallbacks do not degrade correctness or developer ergonomics.

Goals:
- Produce a refreshed compatibility matrix that explicitly documents tokenizer tokenization parity, context-window semantics (truncation/prefix handling), KV cache layout/versioning, and function-calling schema compatibility between primary and fallback variants.
- Expand CI vetter that runs sample prompts and structured-output tests across all fallback pairings (primary -> fallback) for the common model families we serve.
- Implement runtime pre-flight checks and a soft-gating flag: when a fallback variant fails parity checks the router will prefer alternate compatible variants or escalate to a graceful degraded response path.
- Automate daily smoke validation of routing-critical pairs and surface regressions to the Console with diffs and sample mismatches.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Compatibility matrix updated and checked in at: gs://redwood-inference/compat-matrices/variant_compat_2026-03.csv and linked from the README. The CSV must include columns: primary_variant, fallback_variant, tokenizer_version, context_effects, kv_layout_hash, function_call_schema_hash, tooling_notes.
2) CI vetter runs in < 30 min for the golden prompt set and asserts parity thresholds (tokenization 100% or flagged reason; structured output schema conformance >= 95%).
3) Router includes a new telemetry tag (router.fallback_verifier_status) and runtime soft-gate logic behind feature flag route_fallback_verifier. Default behavior is to attempt fallback but log mismatches; enable staged gating once matrix is green.
4) Dashboard: Console shows per-variant pair health and a sample prompt diff in the rollouts page for 30 days after rollout.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting tokenizer implementations. This is an ops/compat effort not a model engineering rewrite.
- Full migration of all obscure legacy variants—focus on top 25 most-used fallback pairings by traffic.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Inventory and matrix generation script. Export current variant metadata (tokenizer versions, context window config, kv-layout metadata, tool contract hashes).
- Week 1-2: Build and land CI vetter harness that can spin up a golden set of prompts across variants and produce machine-readable diffs. Add as a nightly job.
- Week 2: Add router soft-gate flag and telemetry hooks; add feature-flag controlled failover policy.
- Week 3: Console integration for the matrix and per-pair diffs, alerting on regression rate > 0.5% for critical pairs.
- Ongoing: Run remediation playbook for flagged pairs (tokenizer alignment, tooling adapters, or model substitution).

Testing strategy:
- Golden prompts: curated set (~120 prompts) covering code, chat, embeddings-like text, and function-calling examples.
- Token-level tokenizer parity: round-trip tokenization + decode + stable hash.
- KV cache parity tests: verify cache key namespace and expected KV hit/miss semantics for truncated prefixes.
- Structured output validation: run JSON schema checks and a small fuzzy matching runner for free-form outputs.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: CI vetter runtime blowup as pair count grows. Mitigation: prioritize top-25 pairs, sample prompts, and do full sweep weekly instead of nightly.
- Risk: False positives from nondeterministic model outputs. Mitigation: use schema-based and tokenization checks as primary signals; textual diffs are advisory.

Deliverables:
- compatibility CSV in the canonical bucket, checked-in generator script in infra/repos/compat-vetter, and a README.
- CI job: infra/ci/vetter-nightly in our GitHub org.
- Router change: PR #/link below, feature flag gate.
- Console panel: Console ticket and short UX mock linked in attachments.

Notes on scope-specific tooling parity:
- Function-calling: compare declared function signatures and required/optional argument handling; add an adapter shim in the router when only minor differences exist (e.g., optional param name changes).
- SDK expectations: ensure JS/py SDKs receive same wire-format when routed to fallback; add end-to-end test with SDK bindings.
- Metrics: add per-pair mismatches metric and sample_id tagging to trace mismatches back to requests.
